Validate a user-supplied ACS tract table

Source: R/checks.R
cacs_acs_validate.Rd

Checks that a user-supplied American Community Survey (ACS) sf tibble (a spatial data frame of census tracts) meets the schema catchmentACS expects before you feed it to cacs_run(). The six checks are: the object is an sf object; its coordinate reference system is NAD83 (EPSG:4269); the required columns are present; every GEOID is an 11-digit tract identifier; estimate and moe (margin of error) are numeric; and the table has at least one row. Run this before calling cacs_run(acs = my_sf, ...) with your own pre-fetched ACS data.

Usage

cacs_acs_validate(x)

Arguments

x

An ACS tract sf tibble.

Value

Invisibly TRUE on success; aborts with a catchmentACS_error_schema condition on the first failed check.

See also

cacs_acs_prefetch() for fetching a schema-valid ACS table, cacs_intersect_weight() and cacs_run() for the consumers that require this schema, and cacs_validate_iso() for the isochrone-side counterpart.

Other validation and conditions: cacs_capture_conditions(), cacs_validate_iso(), cacs_validate_osrm_endpoint(), catchmentACS-conditions

Examples

acs <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "sample_alabama_subset.rds",
                           package = "catchmentACS"))
cacs_acs_validate(acs)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
my_acs <- tidycensus::get_acs(
  geography = "tract", variables = "B01003_001",
  state = "AL", year = 2023, geometry = TRUE, output = "tidy"
)
cacs_acs_validate(my_acs)
} # }
